title: Crewed Capsule: Vostok 1
body:
Crewed Capsule: Vostok 1 carried Yuri Gagarin on the first human spaceflight on 12 April 1961, a single orbit of Earth lasting 108 minutes. Vostok 1 proved that a human could survive launch, weightlessness, and re-entry, and it opened the human space age.

Vostok 1 is a public fact of world history, and Gagarin's flight remains the founding moment of crewed spaceflight.

title: Apollo Lunar Spacecraft
body:
Apollo Lunar Spacecraft carried astronauts to the Moon, with a command module for the crew and a lunar module for landing. Apollo 11 landed the first humans on the Moon on 20 July 1969, and six Apollo missions landed twelve astronauts on the lunar surface.

Apollo is the most celebrated spacecraft program in history, and its achievements define the Space Age.

title: Space Shuttle Orbiter
body:
Space Shuttle Orbiter was a reusable crewed spacecraft flown by NASA from 1981 to 2011, launched like a rocket and landed like an aeroplane. The Shuttle built much of the International Space Station, serviced the Hubble Space Telescope, and carried over eight hundred people to orbit.

The Space Shuttle is a public icon of reusable spaceflight, and its orbiters are now museum pieces visited by millions.

title: Space Station Module
body:
Space Station Module is a pressurised module of an orbital station, providing living, working, and laboratory space for crews over months. The International Space Station, assembled from modules launched by several nations, has been continuously occupied since November 2000.

Space station modules are humanity's outposts in orbit, and their continuous occupation is a quiet triumph of cooperation.

title: Communications Satellite
body:
Communications Satellite is an uncrewed spacecraft in geostationary or other orbits that relays television, telephone, and internet signals across continents. Communications satellites made global broadcasting and long-distance calling ordinary, and they are the invisible infrastructure of modern media.

Communications satellites are the most commercially important spacecraft type, and their signals reach billions daily.

title: Earth Observation Satellite
body:
Earth Observation Satellite is an uncrewed spacecraft carrying cameras and sensors that watch Earth for weather, mapping, farming, disaster response, and climate science. Earth observation satellites such as Landsat, flying since 1972, give humanity a continuous picture of its own planet.

Earth observation satellites are the planet's watchers, and their data guides farming, rescue, and climate policy.

title: Planetary Probe
body:
Planetary Probe is an uncrewed spacecraft sent to explore other planets, moons, and small bodies, carrying cameras and instruments across interplanetary space. Planetary probes such as Voyager 1, now in interstellar space, and the Mars rovers have transformed our picture of the solar system.

Planetary probes are humanity's farthest travellers, and their findings are the raw material of planetary science.

title: Cargo Spacecraft
body:
Cargo Spacecraft is an uncrewed spacecraft built to deliver supplies, food, water, and equipment to a space station, docking automatically or by robotic arm. Cargo spacecraft such as SpaceX Dragon and Northrop Grumman's Cygnus keep the International Space Station supplied.

Cargo spacecraft are the delivery vans of orbit, and their regular flights keep crewed stations alive.
